newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller says $3-bln IMF support possible.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller says $3-bln IMF support possible.

text.p: Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller said on Monday a planned medium-term economic programme would make it possible for Turkey to raise $3 billion through the International Monetary Fund, Anatolian news agency said.
"As of today it appears possible that resources of $3 billion can be raised from the IMF in the context of a medium-term programme," it quoted her as telling reporters.

An IMF delegation visited Turkey in April for a fortnight of talks which focused on the country's chronic problems in the fields of public finance and inflation. Turkey posted a budget deficit of $1.3 billion last year and year-on-year inflation stood at 77.2 percent in April.
Those talks did not yield a stand-by accord, but Ankara indicated that it would seek support from international organisations for its future financial plans.
"In our contacts with the IMF it emerged that a medium-term programme would be very beneficial," she said.
Ciller said the programme would encompass acceleration of privatisation, reform of the costly social security system and the realisation of justice in the tax system.
She also said World Bank officials would visit Turkey soon for talks.
"Work is continuing on raising to $1 billion the credit amount of $650 million made in our first contacts," she said.
